I was very skeptical at first, especially with some of the mixed (and most likely biased) reviews I've seen online, but I love this game. I've only played it for 9 hours, but this game has given me that "new game excitement" that a lot of these other recent games have been missing. There are a lot of cool features; the emotions are super realistic, there is plenty of opportunity for amazing storytelling, and the game overall looks stunning.  

My main criticisms I have at the moment other than some of the bugs and glitches are that "create a Zoi" has a bit of a leaning curve, but there are lots of tutorials to help with that. The Zois have a variety of moodlets and different emotions and reactions, but I feel like the Zois don't hold on to them long enough for my liking, and along with that, it's difficult to slow-build relationships; it's too easy to become soulmates or BFFs with another Zois.  

Either way, I do not regret my purchase at all, and I am VERY excited to see how the final product plays.

As an avid sims player since childhood, I am very happy with this game so far. I haven't even downloaded the sims on my new computer yet because of my experience with Inzoi. Although this game is still in early access, the developers seem dedicated to updating the game as frequently as possible. They are also NOT money hungry (at this stage) unlike EA. They listen to the concerns/recommendations of their player-base, and are more than willing to implement the communities additions into the game. I have encountered a few bugs, but nothing detrimental to my gaming experience thus far. I am very happy with the character creation, and building homes is just as detailed and fun. The gameplay is lacking in some areas, but overall, it's far more interesting than any sims playthrough I have committed myself to in the past. The modding community is great, and I love that the game shows you what needs updating upon boot. I'm excited to see how this game develops further down the line! (Please note, if you're looking for a game that is exactly like the sims, you may be disappointed. Only buy this game if you are looking for a gaming experience that isn't meant to mirror any other games! Inzoi is in it's own class of life simulation)
Everything the sims 4 should have been and more, some problems on lower spec pcs but playable.

I've been having a lot of fun with inZOI. What I enjoy most is being able to create an entire world rather than just focusing on one Zoi or one household.

 I've built my own town in Bliss Bay, where every household has their own home, personality, career, relationships, businesses, and story. I love being able to connect those households together and create a world where what happens to one family can eventually affect another. That kind of storytelling is what keeps me coming back. 

The character creator and build tools give me a lot of freedom, and I really enjoy the open-world aspect, relationships, careers, businesses, customization, and all the little details that make my town feel like its own place.

There are definitely systems I'd like to see become deeper and more interactive, but I also like knowing that the developers are continuing to add and expand the game. With the features they already have planned for future updates, I'm excited to see how the experience continues to grow. 

For me, inZOI is at its best when I'm creating my own stories instead of following a predetermined one. I can spend hours building a household, developing their relationships, setting up their careers, creating their home, and then seeing how they fit into the rest of my town.

I'm really enjoying what inZOI offers right now, and I'm excited to keep building world as new features are added.

Early Access does not mean it should be entirely filled with game-breaking bugs, horrible graphics with terrible pop in's and taking into consideration of the horrible optimisation. I've played many games with bad ports but inZOI takes the crown for being the worst at it's core.

Look I appreciate the scale and the ambition of the devs as to what they have tried to make this game into, but I have to be honest and genuinely say, this game has too many problems and the problems outweigh the positives of the game at the moment.

Buy at your own risk.

inZOI has quickly become one of my favorite games to just get cozy and disappear into for a few hours. 

There’s something so relaxing about putting on some music, making a cute Zoi, decorating their home, picking out outfits, exploring the city and creating little stories for them. I can literally spend HOURS just customizing things and taking cute screenshots.

The game is also absolutely gorgeous. The lighting, environments and little details make everything feel so pretty and cozy, especially when you’re just wandering around with no real objective and letting your Zoi live their little life.

One of my favorite things is that I don’t feel like I have to play a certain way. Sometimes I want to actually progress my Zoi’s life, and other times I just want to decorate, change outfits, take pictures or make a completely new character because I thought of another aesthetic. 

It’s still growing and there are definitely things I’d love to see added in the future, but I’m already having so much fun with what’s here. I’m really excited to see what inZOI becomes as they continue updating it.

If you’re someone who loves cozy games, character customization, decorating, photography and making your own little stories, I definitely recommend it. 🩵

Basically: make a cute Zoi, grab a cozy drink, put on your favorite playlist and suddenly it’s 3 AM.

Bonus: The only DLC that is out at the time of this is COMPLETELY free!

The only downside the game has, I think, is the general lack of content. What is there, though, is a lot for an early access game; and there are regular updates that add even more. The dev team is very communicative and they try hard to keep players in the loop about what they're working on and what's upcoming.

This game has improved drastically since initial early access release. When I first tried it at the start of early access, it felt boring, buggy, and shallow... but now they have made so many good changes, it's now an actual life simulation game with lots of nice features, including features not found in others. I'm able to create actual characters that feel like people now. 

I really love that we can toggle to directly control the movement by pressing the Tab key, and walk/run around freely. Driving is also fun. One of the biggest downsides currently is that you can't fully edit Zois who are already in-world (and currently no mods exist to get around it). I hope they will allow it in the future.

I the value is great for what content and features are available in just the base game and free DLC. I am looking forward to seeing more progress.

I was so excited for this game long before it was released, and bought it the day it went on sale. And I will admit that it was pretty enjoyable for the first few times I played, but there is a big feeling of it all being very shallow and surface level. There's very little actual "playability" to it. Basically: it looks quite good, but essentially has no depth or personality to it. 

And on top of that... the use of AI. At first I justified it to myself because I thought the AI would remain an "optional" part of the experience, with users choosing whether or not they want to use the generation tools. However, seeing as this is a Korean game and Korean's have a weird obsession with shoehorning AI into every facet of their lives and products, I should have expected that wouldn't be the case. I wish companies would realize that players do not want more AI shoved down their throat. Give us real art that you are proud to make and that players will be proud to play. There are also no excuses to use it during the production process of the game, unless you just want to be cheap and lazy. 

TLDR: I had huge hopes for this game since it was first announced, but it's unfortunately a soulless, AI-heavy product in a somewhat nice-looking (yet often glitchy) package.

As a long-time player of The Sims 3 and 4 (unfortunately my playtime isn't reflected on this account) starting 2016, Inzoi is truly one of the few competitors that can actually stand toe-to-toe with it. 

To preface, I don't want this review to simply be a comparison chart with the Sims, that's not my intention. I think Inzoi itself even without comparing it to competitors is a great game. These comparisons only serve as a benchmark that those unfamiliar with this game but are familiar with the Sims can compare it to.

But ultimately, what keeps me coming back to the game is how alive it feels. While the Sims 3 had the open world and rich characters to it, and Sims 4 had the random events, random encounters, and all sorts of live events, Inzoi manages to take the open world aspect and some of the character depth from Sims 3, and combines it with the various random stuff that the Sims 4 throws at you, on top of the gorgeous visuals, dynamic weather, actual public spaces that have people, and systems such as the phone that really make you feel like you're living a life. Not just simulating it. 

As for the actual breakdown of the good vs bad features:
The Good:
- Of course, the graphics, animations, and the UI. This is one of the strongest parts of the game. it simply looks beautiful, especially on higher settings. While the more realistic nature could turn some people off, especially those more accustomed to the Sims 4 and Paralives, I personally prefer this style. The various lighting effects, ray tracing, and the overall styling really sets the different worlds apart from another very well and gives off a certain atmosphere that just isn't present in those games. And the UI is also quite good. Everything you need is accessible at a glance, I had no problems trying to find anything, its sleek, and importantly, its customisable. You can move different boxes around. Though it would be nice if they could also be resized or rotated. 

- The calendar system and planning system is great. Really helps planning things or setting things up on the fly. I don't usually set up events such as parties or weddings in the Sims 4 or 3 because of the jank, but here its plug and play. And the various "stages" of the events with different activities and animations make it feel realistic, unlike those 2 where I have to deliberately make things like the crowd throwing flower petals in the air during weddings happen.

- The dev team is also deserving of high praise. They are VERY transparent, listen to player feedback constantly, and always showcase new features of the game and explain their development decisions in a manner that feels both fair to the players and developers. I really wish this type of transparency and open dialogue is something that developers of all games could take notes from, because it really fosters a loyal player base while simultaneously allowing players to pitch new ideas that genuinely make the game better. 

- Relationships, while not fleshed out fully yet, are quite deep in their own way. I noticed that its actually slightly hard to enter romantic relationships with characters and you have to keep spamming stuff at them to actually get it to work. Not to mention that they actually degrade, so you have to constantly keep up with them through texts or calls or various meetups.

- CAZ gives pretty advanced control over the characters. On par with the Sims 4. The level of granular control granted is a lot, especially if you choose to design beyond the presets.

- Build mode I believe is also pretty good. Very robust tool that has a LOT of stuff even without any DLC or mods. I also appreciate the little details in being able to add stuff like the exhaust part of an AC. I never used build mode a lot in the Sims despite it being very good in the Sims 4. But here, it was very easy to just start building and customising things to your liking, and I think that's one of its strengths. Its a simple tool with a ton of features and pays attention to the little things that make a house realistic, yet doesn't lock anything behind a paywall.

- The jobs are also quite nice. The fact many jobs in the game are fully playable with modeled workplaces with actual things to do deserves praise. If you want a hands-on job experience in a life sim, this is your go to. Though ti does get repetitive after a while.

The Bad:
- The worlds are just too small. It would be fine if they were sized that way but just had more households to select or to play as. I find that I'm excited to explore the different worlds, yet its almost always the same 1-2 parks, 1-2 cafes, 1-2 arcades, etc etc. And there's just not enough people actually living in the world to make it feel like you're actually simulating or building a community. There's only like 6-10 households in a world. While the Sims 4 also had this issue, it was more justifiable because the world wasn't open so naturally you couldn't interact with them to begin with. But here, since it is, it feels simultaneously massive yet too small.

- Multi-generational gameplay is just bad. Performance tanks (in my experience), and its hard to keep track of multiple families because Zois get up to some weird stuff occasionally and they don't actually interact with one another as a family without you activating it. Not to mention, if I want to setup multiple branches of one family, just 3 kids can already fill up 80% of the world's available house slots. Meaning I have to kick out a lot of existing families, which just does not make it feel realistic at all.

- The lack of an apartment system is quite mind-boggling to me. Its either you own the whole floor or you own the whole apartment. You can even build on the empty floors which...just doesn't make any sense. Hopefully they add in this mechanic. I was really expecting something akin to the Sims 4 city living.

- The careers, while I praised previously, still feel shallow. Not to mention, I would've at least liked the option to either rabbit hole or actually participate in the job. Now its either or. And for the ones that are active, its everyday. For the rabbit holes, promotion takes a long time and its only 3 days in a week.

The neutral:
- Performance. The game has either run really poorly or really well. I am not sure whether this is due to my PC, but hopefully they can rectify it in another update. The September update has improved my performance a lot already, so there's that. But the game is nowhere near its launch state. Bugs have mostly been ironed out and I've only encountered a handful of crashes throughout my experience.

- Ai use. I'm not really against AI that much as long as it isn't obtrusive. Here's its just something optional that you can choose to apply when building houses or making Zois for example. But I think the tech itself is just not that refined here. I'm not sure whether AI is even meant to be a headlining feature but I wish they'd either commit to it or strike it out entirely. I just don't see a reason to use it as of now when the manual alternatives are better or just feel less generic. For example, with Smartzoi, its marketed as a way for Zois to feel more realistic and have their actions be influenced by prompts and their personality. But after keeping it on, I barely notice any changes to the gameplay. And in fact, the improved AI and more personality-based character interactions are already something that the recent September updated improved upon, so I really don't know what this feature is for. The AI features sound great and I would use them to speed things up or make it feel more real, but it just doesn't impact gameplay much or is half-baked that I don't really want to use it.

Ultimately, its not perfect. But its refreshing to finally have a life sim that makes me feel like I'm experiencing something genuinely new rather than simply playing a different version of the same formula.

The foundation is there,and I'm very excited to see where it goes.

The longer I play this game, the more things I see wrong with it, not just bugs, but design choices that really confirms my suspicion that this isn't a Life Sim at all.

Pros:
1. Game looks great, has a somewhat 'okay' cartoon filter for those who don't like the realism (but the outside line is a bit sharp).
2. Games runs good (at least on my machine)
3. interesting take on the life sim genre (you can directly control the character with the WASD keys.)
4. clothing layering/texturing/colour wheel are great.
5. Great updates, and it does get a lot of TLC from both modders and the developers which is wonderful to see.

Cons:
1. It has features that uses Gen AI (thankfully you can choose to ignore them, but I would much rather not have it on my machine at all.)
-
2. The 'customisation' of the character creator isn't as expansive as it looks.
a. Visually outfits/hair can be applied to either gender (unless a mod hasn't flagged an object right, but that's on the modder) but the outfits 'fit' on the bodies doesn't always line up right and you can get garments that are so large they clip.
b. gender identity is completely useless; it only impacts pronouns and what bathroom a Zoi uses. The body function is strictly binary to the male/female body type, and what's worse is that the sliders don't even allow you to make butch females or transgender men. You cannot dictate if a Zoi is capable of causing pregnancy/getting pregnant/doing neither.
c. Still on the subject of the gender identity; it is only available to young adults or higher. (you can assign sexual orientation to teenagers but not a gender identity? Why?)
d. You can't add body hair to females at all (they look like dolls with no hair on arms or legs.)
e. underwear for females is just really bad; you only have girly things. nothing for tomboys.
-
3. Problematic stereotyping of genders. This is a huge red flag; if you make a male Zoi their urges are perfectly neutral, but choose a female? Expect to see 'check appearance', 'browse social media', and 'gossip' every few minutes in the urges category. If you leave autonomy on for the female Zoi, they'll be going to take selfies and mess with their hair every few seconds. The idle animations are just as bad; males are pretty neutral, but females jumop around and act like small children, all 'oh look at me i am a fragile little flower so cute make me your waifu wuwu' and stuff when standing around or talking to people, and that stuff is just outright insulting to still see in this day and age.
-
4. The game claims to have 'autonomy off' toggles, but then hijacks control of the Zoi in certain situations anyway; if a Zoi sees a crime, they auto-report it. If a baby cries, the Zoi goes to them. If there's a dance battle or performance, etc nearby, the Zoi will go participate even if they're only passing by/through. The only way to stop this is to force them to walk away or cancel the interaction immediately, but the game constantly keep trying to pull them back to whatever it is. If I turn autonomy off, I expect it to stay off no matter what is happening. (The perception of you having 'complete control' is not at all true.)
-
5. Skills and actions are restricted for certain age groups that should still have them; Teenage delinquency is a real-world thing, but this game treats them as innocent people who can do no wrong other than shout at a teacher or student. There are no real pranks; they cannot obtain the crime skill until they're a young adult, and they cannot commit acts of vandalism/be arrested. This again should be in a Life Sim: teenagers behaving like teenagers, which is to say, being bad and challenging authority, but it isn't.
-
6. Life sims are supposed to simulate life in all its raw, messy ugliness; you are meant to have polar opposites throughout life, not just 'rivals' or 'enemies'. 
a. There are meant to be people who want kids and who don't. Right now the game expects every single Zoi to want a child. (Traits have no impact on family preferences.)
b. People who want to live alone without 'recognition' because they're hermits, and people who can't stand being on their own for five seconds because they constantly need validation. The introvert trait barely does anything remotely akin to what being a real introvert is like (traits have zero impact on needs decay. Introverts should have the recognition need decay super slow, whilst extroverts should have it deplete faster.)
c. People who prefer being around animals over people. (Right now all Zoi's want to constantly be around people, even the introverts, which makes no sense.)
d. You can have entire families fall out, which is great for drama, but the game suffers some form of amnesia; when I make my Zoi a mean POS to their parents, or vice versa, and I make them move out the house, you'd expect them to just sever ties, right? Nope. The father, even after striking his adult son, still sends mushy texts acting as if he hadn't swung a fist. I make my Zoi remove him as a contact, hoping to 'ghost' him, but no; the game still has the POS dad sending his deluded texts. There are zero consequences for bad relationships in the game.
-
7. All the text in this game has clearly been run through a gen-AI system, because it is overly flowery and reads terribly in English. One example is that the game says "It would be best if you no longer pay as much attention to me" in a text that my Zoi sends his parents anytime they disturb him, when a simple "Leave me alone" would have been enough.
a. continuing with the text messages; the game hijacks control of the texting as well. You pick one of three options, the NPC replies, then the game sends another reply to them, then the NPC replies, and only then can you select something else. So when my Zoi tells his abusive parents to 'leave him alone', the parent texts back something, then the game makes my zoi say 'i was just kidding' when he absolutely wasn't kidding, then the POS parent texts back that they are relieved. The game cannot stand genuine family discourse or drama; it must resolve all conflicts itself immediately and gives you zero agency to do it yourself.
-
8. The game adds playtime when you're not even playing it. I know my hours, it's high but not anywhere near as high as what steam is showing. This means the game is still running in the background even when the .exe has been shut down. That behaviour is akin to malware, using my systems resources when I need it for other things, and the developers need to seriously address it.
-
9. THis is just a gripe i have with Life Sims now; smartphone is built into the UI, so there is no incentive or actual rewarding feeling for 'getting one' because it's just there the second your character is born. Also, the Zoi's are always using them, and it's not cute or fun, it's a painful reminder of what a majority of the real world is like; they use them for selfies, in front of mirrors, opn the toilet, lying on the sofa, when walking around... then there's the texting and calling system. I'm amazed nobody else has called them out on all this stuff! Then again, the life sim community has limited options and has been starved for almost two decades, and is probably too scared to say anything. But I'm not; I want a life sim that rivals or surpasses The Sims, and I do want inZoi to do well, but in this current state I do not believe it stands a chance in being The Sims equal, let alone a replacement for it.

Will I still play this game? Sure, but I'm modding it to death just as much as I do the Sims 4, and when a game can only 'work right' when heavily modded, I just can't recommend it. To earn the recommendation, please fix everything in the cons section.

I bought this upon launch, and immediately put it down. While the graphics were beautiful, the game play wasn't there -- particularly how empty and lifeless lots and people felt. I am very ANTI-AI so I was put-off by all the AI bashing that happened with this game. While I've learned it's local AI, and completely up to the player, that along with updates made me dive back into the game. Let's break it down:

Background:

- I've played The Sims since 2000, and have owned every iteration on every console you can think of. I've also played city builders, and spent thousands of hours crafting worlds in various games. Paralives isn't something I've played yet so I can't compare them -- nor would I. Paralives is closer To The Sims 4 and Tomadatchi Life, where Inzoi is closer to The Sims 3 and Grand Theft Auto.

Immersion, Gameplay, and Graphics:

- The gameplay is substantially improved. From crowds in night clubs, to weddings running smoothly, I've got 2 businesses going and employees actually hold DOWN the businesses and I'm profitable. The Zoi family I'm playing husband works at a Press Shop, and it's awesome popping into to say hi to him while he's on lunch while my other Zoi is checking up on her businesses. Stopping and seeing all the other Zois at the architect firm, Deli, etc, working and living their lives is truly immersive. 

- Immersion and graphics go hand in hand in this game. I love playing AS my character, but like the option to be able to hover over like a traditional life sim. Still, directly being able to control my Zoi has taken this immersion to the next level. 

- Facial expressions are largely improved, but yes people still have perpetual botox it seems. Animations are so much better, and funny. Passionate romance animations make me want to give my Zoi's some privacy, while fighting ones are hilarious in a grand theft auto kind of way. 

My FAVORITE experience is living in this little corner of an older K-Town neighborhood in Dowon, and having the playground nearby and a coffee vendor. Getting coffee on my Zoi's way to work is so fun, and then seeing all the kids with their backpacks actively walk to school and wait at crosswalks melted my heart. 

Some features are half-baked, yes, because it's early access, -- keep using the ones you like and let's see them get worked on. Kjun (developer) has been doing a great job at improving existing systems while introducing new ones. Some aren't for me, but I'm glad players are getting MORE options. 

Room for improvement:

- Build mode is obviously still clunky, but you can build some truly breathtaking things. It will take you longer than The Sims and you can't achieve as much detail because certain things aren't there yet -- comprehensive awnings, columns, more fence options, roof options, etc -- but what you can build is great and being able to match wood up, etc with a colorwheel is wonderful 

- Karma system, neighborhood stories, genetics and family lore, as well as ghosts and supernatural elements, also some half-baked systems to me include retail (although it's very entertaining, it needs more -- but this was a free update in early access to I'm happy so far), careers need more diversity in the day to day interactions -- but again it's like real life, so your zoi may be at their computer 75% of the day just like in real life. 

- Facial expressions and overall goofiness needs to be able to be turned up on a slider like you can relationships and other city / neighborhood things. I kind of want more animated people but the Sims goofiness holds my nostalgia. 

Inzoi is a realism based life sim and it's very good if you give it a chance.

My Hope for inZOI's Future

I really enjoy inZOI because I don't want to control every little thing my Zois do. I actually find scripted storylines boring. What I love is creating a city, giving my Zois homes, jobs, places to socialize, and basic life goals—and then stepping away and letting them live their own lives.

My favorite way to play is more like taking care of a garden. 🌱 I might cook dinner, clean the house, take care of real-life responsibilities, then come back to my game and check on my Zois to see what happened while I was gone. Did they fall in love? Get married? Have a baby? Move into a new house? Make new friends? I want those things to happen naturally without me having to direct everything.

I really hope KRAFTON continues developing inZOI for many years and adds expansions that focus on deeper life simulation and autonomy, not just furniture and clothing.

I would especially love to see:

More natural autonomous dating, marriage, and family formation
Deeper generations, aging, children, and family relationships
Zois being able to independently develop careers and businesses
More meaningful neighborhoods and community life
Pets
Seasons and holidays
More cities and travel
More autonomous decisions and consequences that make the world feel alive
I know not everyone plays this way, and that's okay. But for players like me, the biggest attraction isn't creating a story—it's watching the simulation create its own stories.

I really hope inZOI continues growing into that kind of game. I would happily support expansions that make the world feel more alive and independent.

There's plenty to love:
- You can absolutely make your own fun and feel like you're creating your own stories.
- When it comes to conversations, actions, etc., there are many unique, novel options to choose from (which is very refreshing as a long-time Sims player). If you have "Smart Zoi" features enabled, you'll also run into some truly beautifully unhinged stuff. 
- The graphics are stunning if you have a powerful enough rig to run all the settings at "high" or "ultra." (I have also played this on "medium" on an RTX 4050 laptop and had pretty decent results too, but you WILL be underwhelmed if you're expecting it to look anything like the trailers, promo, average YouTube gameplay vids, etc.)

So why can I not recommend this weird, beautiful game? 
I appreciate the dev team for providing such detailed updates, patch notes, new content info; for taking some feedback into consideration, and I'll give kudos to anyone trying to make a game that can compete with The Sims in a genre it has completely dominated for years. BUT!: 
- There are TOO many issues to make this a consistently fun experience. 
- Glitches and bugs
- Glitches and bugs
- Glitches and bugs
- Regarding the aforementioned lovingly detailed notes from the devs... The content of said notes are usually... A tad mind boggling? Like what? Why are they spending so much time adding a million minor/irrelevant/inconsequential features when half the actual game is busted?? Smooth out the egregious bugs in the CORE gameplay first. I know game dev is a complex process, but it feels like they’re making this game as wide as a lake and deep as a puddle. 
— I understand this a work in progress, but it feels hilarious to read the latest patch notes and they’re like “Note #1: We’re finally working on a basic, integral, core gameplay element that has somehow never been ironed out despite this game existing for as long as it has! Now your Zois will be more likely to sit to eat dinner together in the dining room, instead of walking to the other side of the lot and staring catatonically at a wall while shoveling the contents of their bowl into their mouths!  Note #2: Also now you can scuba dive.”
— New features being added by an update aren't exciting, but only because: Half the updates actually will just make the game crash on launch, and it'll keep being broken until the next patch. I can run almost any modern game on 1440p resolution on high settings at 50-70 FPS, with NO issues. But this one just s***s its pants. 
- Why do updates basically delete your saves and wipe your progress? What?? Hey in case anyone hasn't told the devs this: Don't! It sucks and is super boring?? I'm actively yawning typing this. I understand mods being disabled after patches, but it blows to have all your non-modded creations and progress obliterated. 
- I can't actually list all the frustrating/game-breaking bugs + missing/broken features without crashing out or hitting the word limit, whichever comes first.

I usually like this game. Someday I may even love it! But for now, I can just take whatever crumbs of joy I can extract from it and ride that wave until a game-breaking bug or progress-resetting update makes me rage quit for a few months; then I'll inevitably get enticed by them adding some random stupid feature like armpit hair braiding or horse daycare or realistic toilet splash sounds, and forget why I initially stopped playing and hop back on. Then immediately run into the same !@#$ issues, ad infinitum!

Anyway, tldr, 6/10, devs gotta fix the persistent bugs plaguing the core gameplay before adding so many misc features and stop breaking a game that seems to be precariously running atop a house of cards

Inzoi: Life Sim in Need of Polish - Early Access Review
Verdict: Inzoi, the new life simulation game from Krafton, shows incredible potential and justifies its price point for enthusiasts eager to jump into a fresh take on the genre. However, as an Early Access title released on March 28, 2025, it undeniably requires significant work to reach its full potential and stand confidently as a true competitor in the market.
The Good:
Stunning Visuals: Powered by Unreal Engine 5, Inzoi is a visually impressive game. The character models are detailed, and the environments, while sometimes feeling a bit empty, are aesthetically pleasing. The level of customization in the "Create A Zoi" mode is extensive, allowing for the creation of truly unique characters with diverse features, hairstyles, and clothing options.
Deep Customization: Beyond characters, the building and decoration tools offer a vast array of options. Players can adjust everything from wall sizes and textures to furniture placement and even customize furniture patterns using text prompts and image inputs via on-device generative AI. This level of personalization is a significant strength.
Ambitious Features: Inzoi aims to deliver a comprehensive life simulation experience with features like an open world (across three distinct cities inspired by Korea, the US, and Indonesia), a karma system influencing gameplay, drivable cars, and the ability to manage city-wide aspects like weather and social dynamics. The inclusion of a detailed schedule system for your "Zois" (the game's characters) to automate routines is a welcome touch.
Active Development and Roadmap: Krafton has been transparent about their development plans, providing a roadmap for 2025 that includes significant updates. Planned additions include body customization, pets (cat companions in August 2025), swimming pools, playable ghosts, modding support, new cities, cheat codes, and much more. This commitment to ongoing development is encouraging.
Positive Early Reception: Despite its flaws, Inzoi has garnered a "Very Positive" rating on Steam from early access players, indicating that the core concepts and potential are resonating with the audience. Many appreciate the fresh approach and the detailed customization options.
The Needs Improvement:
Gameplay Depth and Cohesion: While visually appealing and feature-rich on paper, the gameplay in its current state feels somewhat bare-bones and lacks meaningful progression. Many reviewers note that beyond the extensive customization, there isn't a strong sense of purpose or engaging activities to pursue. The world can feel like a stage for beautiful characters without enough compelling interactions or scenarios.
UI and Controls: Some players have reported that the user interface can be clunky and unintuitive, particularly in the build mode, making it difficult to place objects and construct complex designs. Pathing for the Zois can also appear unnatural.
Simulation Quirks: As with many early-access life sims, Inzoi has its share of oddities and bugs. Reports include overly fast relationship progression, a lack of meaningful consequences, and some unexpected character behaviors.
Performance and Optimization: While some users report smooth performance, others, especially those aiming for the highest graphical settings, may encounter performance issues. The minimum and recommended specs suggest a relatively powerful PC is needed to fully appreciate the visual fidelity.
Missing Features: As an early access title, many expected features are still missing or in experimental stages. For example, while pets are planned, they are not currently available. The AI "Smart Zoi" feature, intended to provide deeper insights into character thoughts and actions, is still under development.
World Engagement: While the ability to edit the city is present, some players feel that the pre-made indoor venues lack customizability, limiting the sense of truly shaping the world. Additionally, the world can sometimes feel static and lacking in dynamic events beyond those directly triggered by the player.
Is it Worth the Price?
For players who are passionate about life simulation games, enjoy deep customization options, and are willing to experience a game in its early stages with the understanding that significant improvements are needed and planned, Inzoi is likely worth the price of admission. The visual fidelity and the sheer breadth of customization are genuinely impressive and offer a unique experience.
However, if you are looking for a polished and feature-complete life simulation game with deep, engaging gameplay loops right out of the box, it might be prudent to wait for further updates and the full release. Keep an eye on the development roadmap and player feedback to see how the game evolves over the coming months.
In Conclusion:
Inzoi has laid a promising foundation with its stunning graphics and extensive customization. The developers at Krafton clearly have a strong vision for the game. However, the early access version highlights the significant work that remains to be done in terms of gameplay depth, simulation refinement, and overall polish. If Krafton continues to actively listen to player feedback and deliver on their ambitious roadmap, Inzoi has the potential to become a true contender in the life simulation genre. For now, it's an exciting glimpse into what could be, with the caveat that it's still very much a work in progress.
